report.headline: Do not sign this lease as written: it contains multiple terms that conflict with Connecticut tenant protections.
report.summary: The most urgent issue is the lease, which includes several terms the reviewer says are prohibited or unenforceable under Connecticut law. Public records also leave the ownership chain unclear, and the building and nearby area have some items worth asking about. Request corrected lease terms in writing before signing; this is not legal advice, and a free legal aid service can help with the lease concerns.

findings.title: Security deposit exceeds legal maximum
findings.detail: The lease demands $5,400, equal to three months' rent, while the calculated maximum for a tenant under 62 is $3,600. The excess $1,800 is above Connecticut's limit; ask for the deposit to be reduced. If you are 62 or older, the permitted limit is lower still.

findings.title: Late fee starts too early and is too high
findings.detail: The lease imposes a fee after four days and charges $100 plus $10 per additional day. Connecticut requires a nine-day grace period for monthly rent and limits a single late fee to the lesser of $5 per day up to $50 or 5% of late rent; this clause is unenforceable to the extent it conflicts with those limits.

findings.title: Application and move-in fees are prohibited
findings.detail: The lease charges a $150 application processing fee and a $250 move-in fee. Connecticut prohibits these fees; only specified charges, including a qualifying tenant screening report fee, are allowed, so ask that both charges be removed.

findings.title: Heat surcharge conflicts with included heat
findings.detail: The lease says heat is included in rent but also requires a $75 monthly heating surcharge from November through March. Connecticut prohibits a heat or utility surcharge when that service is included in the lease, so ask to remove the surcharge.

findings.title: Tenant made responsible for all repairs
findings.detail: The lease makes you responsible for every repair, including plumbing, heating, and electrical systems, regardless of cause. That broad transfer conflicts with the landlord's statutory repair and habitability duties and is unenforceable to that extent; ask for the clause to preserve the landlord's required duties.

findings.title: Entry allowed without notice or limits
findings.detail: The landlord claims a right to enter at any time, without notice, for any purpose. Connecticut generally requires reasonable notice and reasonable times, with entry without consent limited to specified circumstances; ask for the clause to be replaced with a lawful entry provision.

findings.title: Lockout and property removal without court
findings.detail: The lease purports to let the landlord change the locks and remove your belongings without court action. A landlord may not dispossess a tenant without a court order, making this clause unenforceable; ask that it be deleted.

findings.title: Landlord liability waiver and indemnity
findings.detail: The lease attempts to excuse the landlord from liability even for the landlord's negligence and makes you indemnify the landlord for all such claims. Connecticut prohibits waiving or shifting the landlord's legal liability this way, so ask to remove this clause.

findings.title: Waiver of statutory tenant rights
findings.detail: The lease says you waive all rights and remedies under Chapter 830. Connecticut prohibits lease terms that waive tenant protections under landlord-tenant statutes, and the waiver is unenforceable; ask for it to be removed.

findings.title: Attorney fees are not limited
findings.detail: The lease requires you to pay all of the landlord's attorney's fees and collection costs in full in any dispute. Connecticut bars requiring attorney's fees above 15% of a judgment for money damages in the circumstances covered by the statute; ask for the clause to be limited to the statutory rule.

findings.title: Electronic-only rent payment
findings.detail: The lease requires automatic electronic debit and rejects checks and money orders. Connecticut prohibits requiring electronic funds transfer as the only rent-payment method; ask for a non-electronic payment option.

findings.title: Ownership chain not fully identified
findings.detail: The registry lists SFR 2 DE Pledgor LLC as a principal of SFR 2 DE LLC, but a Connecticut registry search returned no match for that principal. The available records therefore do not identify the people or further entities behind it.

findings.title: Older building; average condition
findings.detail: The assessor records the building as built in 1880 and in Average condition. Ask about recent plumbing, electrical, heating, and roof work, and what repairs are planned.

findings.title: Three reports logged at the address
findings.detail: The address itself had reports for a parking violation, a dead squirrel, and a stolen catalytic converter; the theft report is listed as open. These reports do not establish a building problem, but ask about any recent security or pest issues and inspect the immediate area.

findings.title: Large Connecticut portfolio
findings.detail: The owner holds 127 Connecticut parcels across 3 towns, with 113 in New Haven. Ask who handles repairs at this building, how maintenance requests are tracked, and who is authorized to respond locally.

findings.title: Nearby trash and dumping complaints
findings.detail: The 311 results show 11 illegal-dumping reports and 23 missed-trash/recycling reports across the search area, with several reports on nearby Wooster and Olive streets. Ask how trash is handled and check the block for recurring dumping or overflow.

findings.title: Owner is an active LLC
findings.detail: SFR 2 DE LLC is listed as the property owner and has Active registry status. Its registry mailing address is in Woodbridge, while the assessor lists a New Haven mailing address; confirm which address is best for notices and maintenance requests.

CT-47a-4-a1.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(1): Waiving tenant rights
CT-47a-4-a1.data: A lease may not make the tenant waive or forfeit rights or remedies under the landlord-tenant statutes (or other statutes and ordinances, unless that law expressly allows waiver). Such a clause is unenforceable (§ 47a-4(b)).

CT-47a-4-a2.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(2): Confession of judgment
CT-47a-4-a2.data: A lease may not authorize the landlord to confess judgment against the tenant on a claim arising from the lease.

CT-47a-4-a3.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(3): Landlord liability waivers and indemnity
CT-47a-4-a3.data: A lease may not make the tenant agree to excuse or limit the landlord's legal liability, or to indemnify the landlord for that liability or its costs.

CT-47a-4-a4.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(4): Interest on security deposit
CT-47a-4-a4.data: A lease may not make the tenant waive the right to interest on the security deposit under § 47a-21.

CT-47a-4-a5.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(5): Lockouts / eviction without court
CT-47a-4-a5.data: A lease may not let the landlord remove (dispossess) the tenant without a court order.

CT-47a-4-a6.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(6): Seizing tenant property for rent
CT-47a-4-a6.data: A lease may not make the tenant consent to the landlord seizing (distraining) the tenant's property for unpaid rent.

CT-47a-4-a7.data: A lease may not make the tenant pay the landlord's attorney's fees above 15 percent of any judgment against the tenant in a case where money damages are awarded.

CT-47a-4-a8.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(8): Late fee before grace period / early-payment 'discounts'
CT-47a-4-a8.data: A lease may not charge a late fee before the statutory grace period ends, or set rent as a 'discounted' amount if paid before the grace period ends.

CT-47a-4-a9.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(9): Late fee amount
CT-47a-4-a9.data: A lease may not charge a late fee larger than the limits in § 47a-15a.

CT-47a-4-a10.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4(a)(10): Heat or utility surcharge
CT-47a-4-a10.data: If heat or utilities are included in the lease, the lease may not add a heat or utilities surcharge.

CT-47a-15a-a.data: Rent is not considered late for termination purposes until 9 days after it is due (4 days for a week-to-week tenancy). This 9-day (or 4-day) window is the 'grace period'.

CT-47a-15a-b.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-15a(b): Late fee cap
CT-47a-15a-b.data: A late fee may be charged only after the grace period and may not exceed the lesser of (1) $5 per day up to a maximum of $50, or (2) 5 percent of the late rent payment. Only one late fee may be charged per late payment, however long it stays unpaid.

CT-47a-16.data: Except in an emergency, the landlord must give reasonable written or oral notice before entering and may enter only at reasonable times. The landlord may not abuse the right of entry or use it to harass the tenant. Without the tenant's consent, entry is allowed only in an emergency, under § 47a-16a (extended absence), with a court order, or if the unit is abandoned.

CT-47a-4d.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4d: Application, screening, move-in and move-out fees
CT-47a-4d.data: A landlord may not charge a prospective tenant any fee to process, review or accept a rental application, and may not charge move-in or move-out fees. The only up-front charges allowed are a security deposit, first month's rent, a key or special-equipment deposit, and a tenant screening report fee capped at $50 (adjusted annually for inflation by the Commissioner of Housing). A landlord who charges a screening fee must give the tenant a copy of the report (or how to get it) and the receipt.

CT-47a-4c.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4c: Electronic-only rent payment
CT-47a-4c.data: For leases signed on or after October 1, 2013, a landlord may not require electronic funds transfer as the only way to pay rent or the security deposit.

CT-47a-4e.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-4e: Rent increase notice
CT-47a-4e.data: A rent increase is not effective unless the landlord gives written notice at least 45 days before it takes effect (for leases of one month or less, notice equal to one full lease term). A tenant's silence is not agreement. This does not allow raising rent during the lease term.

CT-47a-6.data: By the start of the tenancy the landlord must tell the tenant in writing the name and address of the person managing the premises and the person authorized to receive notices and legal papers, and keep that information current.

CT-47a-7.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-7(a): Landlord repair duties
CT-47a-7.data: The landlord must follow building and housing codes affecting health and safety; make repairs to keep the premises fit and habitable; keep common areas clean and safe; maintain electrical, plumbing, sanitary, heating, ventilating and other supplied facilities and appliances; provide trash receptacles and removal; and supply running water, reasonable hot water and reasonable heat (unless these are under the tenant's exclusive control or supplied by a direct utility connection). Shifting duties to the tenant is limited: for a single-family home, a good-faith written agreement may have the tenant handle trash, water/heat supply and specified repairs (§ 47a-7(c)); for other units, a good-faith written agreement may have the tenant do specified repairs or maintenance only if the work is not needed to fix code violations or make the unit habitable, and it does not reduce the landlord's duties to other tenants (§ 47a-7(d)).

CT-47a-21-b.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(b): Security deposit maximum
CT-47a-21-b.data: A landlord may not demand a security deposit of more than two months' rent from a tenant under 62, or more than one month's rent from a tenant 62 or older.

CT-47a-21-d.source: Conn. Gen. Stat. § 47a-21(d)(2): Security deposit return deadline
CT-47a-21-d.data: After the tenancy ends, the landlord must return the deposit plus accrued interest (or the balance with a written, itemized list of damages deducted) within 21 days, or within 15 days of receiving the tenant's written forwarding address, whichever is later.
